clue.text: Show match that can be used to select player

definitions.text: that can be used to select player

parts.note: to show a film is to screen it
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: Someone describes a trial game arranged so selectors can pick a player.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby, so 'match' gives TEST; the 'player' sought is an actor, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A film studio judges a would-be actor by a trial filming before casting them.

clue.text: Pack carefully for school, say

indicators.note: say signals that the school's name is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Stowe is an English public school in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child to pack their trunk neatly for boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: STOWE is a well-known English boarding school; spoken, it matches the word for packing away.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things away neatly and compactly, as luggage in a hold.

clue.text: Girl's ace of diamonds?

definitions.meaning: Babe ..., the great American baseball star, an ace of the baseball diamond

explanation.surface: A woman holds the top card of a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' looks like a card suit, but a baseball field is a diamond; Babe Ruth was its most famous star.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical woman's name, also the surname of the legendary New York Yankees slugger.

clue.text: I repeatedly deal with Tories in order to work with leaders

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh
repeatedly says the single letter is used twice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps having to negotiate with Conservatives to work with their bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives II; with DEAL and TORIES these are rearranged by 'in order'. 'Leaders' are leading articles, newspaper editorials.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper leaders are opinion columns, and writing such opinion pieces is the verb here.

clue.text: Unfinished story about claw

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for story loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A half-told tale concerns a bird's claw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the last letter of the story; 'about' here is the sense 'concerning', as in a book on birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked nail of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Accepts changes to the French exhibition

indicators.note: changes to says the word accepts is rearranged

parts.note: le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to alterations to a French show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes to' rearranges ACCEPTS into SPECTAC; LE is French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking public show or display, something to look at.

clue.text: Mineral outcrop with awful contents removed

indicators.note: with their contents removed, only the first and last letters of each of the two words survive

explanation.surface: A geologist finds a seam of mineral in an outcrop after clearing away nasty debris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents removed' strips both 'outcrop' and 'awful' to their first and last letters: O-P and A-L.
explanation.definitionFit: The gemstone is a form of silica, classed as a mineraloid.

clue.text: Food for beautiful people

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a vision is a strikingly lovely person

explanation.surface: Someone describes catering for a glamorous crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO is Latin-derived 'for'; a 'vision' can be a very beautiful person.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies of things to eat stocked up for a journey.

clue.text: Land with Irish after five in Limerick, say

indicators.note: after puts the word for Irish behind the numeral

parts.note: to light on is to land on
V is the Roman numeral for five
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Ireland and its Irish come after a fifth stop in the city of Limerick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limerick' looks like the Irish city, but a limerick is a comic five-line poem; LIGHT + V + ERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a comic rhyme, an example of humorous poetry.

clue.text: Sportsman in no position to make a slip

definitions.text: Sportsman in no position to make a slip

parts.words: Sportsman in no position to make a slip
parts.note: in cricket a slip is a close catching position beside the wicketkeeper; a fielder stationed far from the bat is in no such position

explanation.surface: An athlete is too far away to commit an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' reads as an error, but in cricket the slips are close fielders beside the wicketkeeper; a fielder out near the boundary is nowhere near that position.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder posted far from the batsman, near the boundary, rather than close in.

clue.text: Secret society singularly lacking grip

indicators.note: made singular, the plural word loses its final S

parts.note: tongs are a tool for gripping

explanation.surface: A clandestine group is said to lack a firm hold.
explanation.walkthrough: TONGS is a plural noun; 'singularly lacking' asks for it without its plural S.
explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret association or brotherhood, sometimes criminal.

clue.text: Representative wheel parts for each boy

parts.note: spokes are the rods of a wheel
per means for each
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A delegate shares out bicycle wheel components among the lads.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOKES + PER + SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks officially on behalf of a group.

clue.text: Either 1dn or 26, in the event

definitions.meaning: STOW runs from S to W and the school at 26 runs from E to N: each goes from one compass point to another
a cross-country steeplechase for amateur riders

explanation.surface: A cross-referencing clue asking which of two other entries fits a certain event.
explanation.walkthrough: The other two entries each start and end on a compass point, S...W and E...N; the same phrase names a British amateur horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Words starting and ending on compass letters go between bearings; the hunting-season steeplechase is named for racing between landmarks.

clue.text: Chairman on one board making money.

parts.note: a professor holds a chair at a university
I is the Roman numeral for one
a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A company chairman sits on a board that turns a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairman' is not a company head but a holder of a university chair, a professor; in a down clue 'on' puts him above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that brings in a good return is lucrative.

clue.text: It confers grace with love in US city

parts.note: in Christian teaching a sacrament is a rite conferring divine grace
love is nil, or O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A religious rite combines with love in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: SACRAMENT + O, with love as zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of California.

clue.text: It is clear it might be practical

indicators.note: might be says these letters could become another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a plain fact may turn out to be useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges the nine letters of 'It is clear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sensible and down-to-earth about what can be achieved is being practical.

clue.text: Such a state, in the end, upsetting one's head?

definitions.text: Such a state, in the end, upsetting one's head?

parts.words: Such a state, in the end, upsetting one's head?
parts.note: a condition brought on by drink that eventually leaves the drinker's head spinning and topples them over

explanation.surface: Someone asks what condition ends up turning a person's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The state is mild drunkenness, which tips one over; 'upsetting' means tipping over, not distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly drunk makes the head swim and the drinker unsteady.

clue.text: Utensil taken back from chef in kitchen

indicators.note: taken back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook's tool is retrieved from a chef working in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EFINK sits across 'chef in kitchen'; 'taken back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladed cutting implement is one of the basic pieces of cutlery.

clue.text: Odd characters -among foes, really savage

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of each word are the odd-numbered ones

explanation.surface: Among one's enemies some strange people are truly vicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' picks F, E from 'foes' and R, A, L from 'really'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal gone untamed is fierce and uncivilised.

clue.text: Birds in bush finally trapped by countrymen

indicators.note: trapped by puts the letter inside the word for country folk

parts.note: peasants are country people working the land

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of bush

explanation.surface: Game birds hiding in the undergrowth are caught by rural folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives H, the end of 'bush', and 'trapped by' puts it inside PEASANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-tailed game fowl shot for sport in the British countryside.

clue.text: Charming females on paper control devices

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the newspaper

parts.note: The Times is a national newspaper
witches cast charms, or spells

explanation.surface: Enchanting women appear in print, maybe in a magazine feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' means casting charms, not attractive; in an across clue 'on' places the females after the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock-driven switches turn heating or lights on and off at set hours.

clue.text: East End singers

definitions.meaning: the part of a church nearest the altar, at the eastern end

explanation.surface: Cockney singers from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' looks like the London district, but it is the eastern end of a church, where the choir stalls stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel area where the church's singers sit shares its name with the vocal group itself.

clue.text: Tool for something joiner does, 'we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is heard, not read, matching another in sound

parts.note: a joiner joins, that is, adds things together

explanation.surface: A carpenter's tool is named for what a joiner does.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'joiner' is a carpenter, but here also one who joins, or adds; ADDS sounds like the woodworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle, used for shaping wood.

clue.text: Left-winger's moderate pace

definitions.meaning: short for a Trotskyist, a follower of Trotsky
a gait between walking and running

explanation.surface: A socialist walks at an unhurried speed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Trot is informal for a Trotskyist, a far-left supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's two-beat gait sits between walk and canter; the political label abbreviates a Trotskyist.

clue.text: Musicians excluded from audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so this signals a word that sounds the same

parts.note: excluded means banned

explanation.surface: Players are turned away after a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a musicians' tryout but here just means hearing: BANNED sounds like the group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of instrumentalists playing together.

clue.text: Change mind about Conservative party? Right

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a side is one party in a dispute or match

explanation.surface: A voter wonders whether to switch away from the Tories, the party of the right.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + CON + SIDE + R; 'party' is one side in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To think again about a decision and possibly alter it.

clue.text: Latin and French one got in school

parts.note: et is the Latin for and
on is the French pronoun meaning one

explanation.surface: Latin and French were learned by someone accepted at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: ET is 'and' in Latin (and in French); ON is the French impersonal pronoun 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Acerbic article dispatched about Herts town

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about puts the word for sent round the town

parts.note: dispatched means sent
Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued newspaper piece was sent off about a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, an English county just north of London; 'about' wraps the dispatched word round the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting and harsh in tone, like a sharply critical remark.
